A proposal from the Trump administration to revise the Endangered Species Act could have critical impacts on vulnerable animals, plants and habitats throughout the U.S., according to environmental advocates.

Earlier this week, the U.S. Department of the Interior outlined several rules within the ESA that it plans to roll back. Included in the proposed revisions are changes to the listing of protected species and critical habitat, which would be based on the "best scientific and commercial data available," according to the Interior Department.

The administration has also proposed changes to the 4(d) provision, which currently casts a blanket protection over threatened species unless federal agencies outline species-specific alternatives. Conservation groups warned that removing that automatic safeguard would make it harder to list species in need, reduce habitat conservation and create loopholes that undermine protections for imperiled wildlife.

The Trump administration is also proposing to restrict the amount of habitats protected under the ESA by narrowing the definition of "critical habitat" to exclude currently unoccupied but historic habitat. Environmental advocates say that could weaken recovery efforts for species that depend on restoring former ranges.

Changes to interagency cooperation rules would also make it easier for federal agencies to greenlight projects such as mining, drilling, logging and overdevelopment without fully assessing impacts on threatened and endangered species or their habitats, according to Defenders of Wildlife.

Since the Endangered Species Act was passed in 1973, it has saved 95% of listed species from extinction since its inception, a study published in 2019 found. The law has long been considered one of the nation's bedrock environmental statutes.

Polling published in June 2025 found that four out of five Americans support the ESA, according to the International Fund for Animal Welfare. A 30-day period of public comment is now in place following the Interior Department's proposal.
